issues.legal_issue: A planning authority cannot exercise town-planning powers over land outside its notified operational area merely because a delegatee later expands the planning area.
material_facts: The authority was constituted for an area defined by an earlier notification, which did not include the disputed villages.
A committee with delegated powers expanded the planning area to include those villages, but had not been delegated the power to expand the authority’s operational area.
The authority declared its intention to prepare a scheme covering the disputed villages before the State formally extended its operational area to include them.
issues.conclusion: The authority’s action concerning land outside its operational area was without jurisdiction and a nullity; the High Court’s decision was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A delegatee must act within the limits of its delegation. The committee’s delegated power to alter a planning area did not include power to expand the operational area of an authority constituted under Section 38. The Court relied on State of Orissa v. Commissioner of Land Records and Settlement, including its discussion of Roop Chand v. State of Punjab, and on Rakesh Vij v. Dr. Raminder Pal Singh Sethi in explaining delegated authority and the distinction between legislation by incorporation and legislation by reference.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_town_planning_authority_action and authority_area_was_limited_by_its_constitutive_instrument and disputed_land_was_outside_that_area and delegate_lacked_power_to_expand_authority_area and no_effective_expansion_had_occurred

predicates.appeal_concerning_town_planning_authorit: The case is an appeal concerning an action taken by a town-planning authority.
predicates.authority_area_was_limited_by_its_consti: The instrument constituting the authority confined its operation to a specified area.
predicates.disputed_land_was_outside_that_area: The land affected by the authority’s action lay outside the area specified in its constitutive instrument.
predicates.delegate_lacked_power_to_expand_authorit: The body that expanded the planning area had not been given power to expand the authority’s operational area.
predicates.no_effective_expansion_had_occurred: No valid expansion of the authority’s operational area had taken effect when it acted.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a town-planning authority action, the authority was confined to a specified area, the land lay outside it, the delegate lacked power to expand it, and no effective expansion had occurred, the action is invalid for lack of jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A town-development scheme intended to implement a development plan cannot be initiated before a final development plan exists.
material_facts: The authority declared its intention to prepare a town-development scheme while the development plan had not attained finality.
The draft development plan had been returned for revision, and a later draft plan was published after the scheme declaration.
The declaration triggered restrictions on land use and development, although the scheme was intended to implement a development plan.
issues.conclusion: A draft development plan is insufficient: the authority may declare its intention to prepare a town-development scheme only in the context of a final development plan. The declaration was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(u), 17, 49, 50 and 53, a town-development scheme implements a development plan, while declaration of intention can impose substantial restrictions on property use. Reading those provisions in context and purposively, the Court held that the plan must be final before the scheme is initiated; a draft plan has no final statutory force. The Court also applied strict construction to restrictions on property rights, relying on T. Vijayalakshmi v. Town Planning Member, State of H.P. v. Rajkumar Brijender Singh, Reserve Bank of India v. Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd., and the property-right principles discussed in State of Uttar Pradesh v. Manohar.

predicates.appeal_concerning_town_development_schem: The case is an appeal concerning the initiation of a town-development scheme.
predicates.no_final_development_plan_existed_when_s: The authority declared its intention to prepare the scheme before a final development plan existed.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a town-development scheme and the authority declared its intention before a final development plan existed, that declaration is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A pending application for building permission creates no vested right to approval, and it must be decided under the law applicable when the authority considers it.
material_facts: An application for permission to develop land remained undecided after it was submitted.
The applicant sought an order requiring the application to be considered under the law applicable at an earlier point, rather than the law applicable when the authority considered it.
The statutory steps required for permission had not been completed, and no permission had been granted on the pending application.
issues.conclusion: The pending application did not confer a vested right to permission, and it must be considered under the law applicable when the authority is called upon to apply its mind to it.
issues.legal_principle: A pending application or settled expectation does not create a vested right to approval before the statutory conditions are satisfied. The application is determined under the law applicable when the authority considers it. The Court relied on Director of Public Works v. Ho Po Sang, Howrah Municipal Corporation v. Ganges Rope Co. Ltd., Union of India v. Indian Charge Chrome, S.B. International Ltd. v. Assistant Director General of Foreign Trade, and Kuldeep Singh v. Government of NCT of Delhi.

predicates.appeal_concerning_pending_permission_app: The case is an appeal concerning a pending application for permission.
predicates.permission_application_remained_undecide: The authority had not decided the permission application.
predicates.statutory_conditions_for_permission_were: The statutory steps required to establish an entitlement to permission had not been completed.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns an undecided permission application and the statutory conditions for permission remain incomplete, the application creates no vested right and is decided under the law applicable when considered.
